index 0000000..64290b6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,287 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Selector expressions and statement-scoped nosec directives.
+
+As in the legacy nosec map, None means no suppression and an empty set
+means blanket suppression. Empty selector results must therefore become None.
+"""
+
+import ast
+import bisect
+import fnmatch
+import re
+import tokenize
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+DIRECTIVE = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-(begin|end|next-line)\b([^#]*)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+SELECTOR_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_*]+|[|&!(),-]")
+
+
+def parse_selector(expression, enabled):
+    """Resolve a selector, using !, then &/- (left to right), then union.
+
+    Whitespace and commas are implicit union operators. Invalid expressions
+    fall back to a union of whitespace/comma-delimited names and IDs.
+    """
+
+    def resolve(token):
+        if token.lower() == "all":
+            return set(enabled)
+        if token.lower() == "none":
+            return set()
+        if re.fullmatch(r"B[0-9]*\*", token, re.IGNORECASE):
+            return fnmatch.filter(enabled, token.upper())
+        test_id = extension_loader.MANAGER.get_test_id(token)
+        return {test_id or token.upper()} & enabled
+
+    if not expression.strip():
+        return set()
+    tokens = []
+    end = 0
+    valid = True
+    for match in SELECTOR_TOKEN.finditer(expression):
+        start = match.start()
+        gap = expression[end:start]
+        if gap.strip():
+            valid = False
+        token = match.group()
+        if tokens and (
+            tokens[-1] == ")" or tokens[-1][0].isalnum() or tokens[-1] == "*"
+        ):
+            if token[0].isalnum() or token in ("(", "!", "*"):
+                if not gap:
+                    valid = False
+                tokens.append("|")
+        tokens.append("|" if token == "," else token)
+        end = match.end()
+    if expression[end:].strip():
+        valid = False
+    position = 0
+
+    def primary():
+        nonlocal position
+        if position >= len(tokens):
+            raise ValueError("Missing operand")
+        token = tokens[position]
+        position += 1
+        if token == "!":
+            return enabled - primary()
+        if token == "(":
+            result = union()
+            if position >= len(tokens) or tokens[position] != ")":
+                raise ValueError("Missing closing parenthesis")
+            position += 1
+            return result
+        if token in ("|", "&", "-", ")"):
+            raise ValueError("Unexpected operator")
+        return set(resolve(token))
+
+    def intersection():
+        nonlocal position
+        result = primary()
+        while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] in ("&", "-"):
+            operator = tokens[position]
+            position += 1
+            operand = primary()
+            result = result & operand if operator == "&" else result - operand
+        return result
+
+    def union():
+        nonlocal position
+        result = intersection()
+        while position < len(tokens) and tokens[position] == "|":
+            position += 1
+            result |= intersection()
+        return result
+
+    try:
+        if not valid:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid selector token")
+        selected = union()
+        if position != len(tokens):
+            raise ValueError("Unexpected token")
+    except (ValueError, RecursionError):
+        selected = set()
+        for token in re.split(r"[\s,]+", expression.strip()):
+            selected.update(resolve(token))
+    if not selected:
+        return None
+    return set() if selected == enabled else selected
+
+
+class NoSecLines(dict):
+    """Legacy inline suppressions plus directives resolved against the AST."""
+
+    def __init__(self, tokens, enabled, parse_inline):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.enabled = enabled
+        self.regions = {}
+        self.next_statements = []
+        self.node_suppressions = {}
+        self.statement_lines = {}
+        self.logical_ends = []
+        comments = {}
+        physical_lines = {}
+        meaningful = []
+        ignored_types = {
+            tokenize.ENCODING,
+            tokenize.ENDMARKER,
+            tokenize.INDENT,
+            tokenize.DEDENT,
+            tokenize.NL,
+            tokenize.NEWLINE,
+            tokenize.COMMENT,
+        }
+        for token in tokens:
+            lineno = token.start[0]
+            if token.type == tokenize.NEWLINE:
+                self.logical_ends.append(lineno)
+            for offset, line in enumerate(token.line.splitlines()):
+                physical_lines[lineno + offset] = line
+            if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
+                directive = DIRECTIVE.search(token.string)
+                if directive:
+                    comments[lineno] = directive
+                else:
+                    self[lineno] = parse_inline(token.string)
+            elif token.type not in ignored_types and token.string not in (
+                "(",
+                ")",
+                "[",
+                "]",
+                "{",
+                "}",
+                ";",
+                "...",
+            ):
+                # AST columns are UTF-8 byte offsets, unlike token columns.
+                column = len(token.line[: token.start[1]].encode("utf-8"))
+                meaningful.append((lineno, column))
+        stack = []
+        for lineno, line in sorted(physical_lines.items()):
+            leading = line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" \t\f"))]
+            indent = len(leading.expandtabs(8))
+            if line.strip():
+                stack = [
+                    (level, tests)
+                    for level, tests in stack
+                    if level == 0 or level <= indent
+                ]
+            directive = comments.get(lineno)
+            kind = directive.group(1).lower() if directive else None
+            if kind == "end" and stack:
+                stack.pop()
+            suppression = self.combine(*(tests for _, tests in stack))
+            if suppression is not None:
+                self.regions[lineno] = suppression
+            if kind == "begin":
+                stack.append((indent, parse_selector(directive[2], enabled)))
+            elif kind == "next-line":
+                index = bisect.bisect_right(meaningful, (lineno, float("inf")))
+                if index < len(meaningful):
+                    self.next_statements.append(
+                        (
+                            meaningful[index],
+                            parse_selector(directive[2], enabled),
+                        )
+                    )
+
+    def combine(self, *suppressions):
+        result = utils.combine_nosec(*suppressions)
+        if result and self.enabled and result >= self.enabled:
+            return set()
+        return result
+
+    def prepare(self, tree):
+        """Bind directives to statements, without leaking into their siblings.
+
+        A compound statement's region span covers its header, excluding its
+        suites. A next-statement directive on a compound statement covers its
+        whole subtree. This keeps region begins inside a suite non-retroactive.
+        """
+        if (
+            not self.regions
+            and not self.next_statements
+            and all(tests is None for tests in self.values())
+        ):
+            return
+        statements = [
+            node for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.stmt)
+        ]
+        spans = {}
+        for node in statements:
+            start = min(
+                [node.lineno]
+                + [d.lineno for d in getattr(node, "decorator_list", [])]
+            )
+            end = node.end_lineno
+            children = []
+
+            def collect_children(parent):
+                for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(parent):
+                    if isinstance(child, ast.stmt):
+                        children.append(child.lineno)
+                    else:
+                        collect_children(child)
+
+            collect_children(node)
+            if children:
+                index = bisect.bisect_left(self.logical_ends, node.lineno)
+                end = self.logical_ends[index]
+            spans[node] = (start, end)
+        next_tests = {}
+        for (line, column), tests in self.next_statements:
+            candidates = [
+                node
+                for node, (start, end) in spans.items()
+                if start <= line <= end
+                and (line != node.lineno or column >= node.col_offset)
+                and (line != node.end_lineno or column < node.end_col_offset)
+            ]
+            if candidates:
+                target = max(
+                    candidates, key=lambda n: (n.lineno, n.col_offset)
+                )
+                next_tests[target] = self.combine(
+                    next_tests.get(target), tests
+                )
+
+        def visit(node, statement_tests=None, inherited_next=None):
+            if isinstance(node, ast.stmt):
+                start, end = spans[node]
+                inherited_next = self.combine(
+                    inherited_next, next_tests.get(node)
+                )
+                statement_tests = self.combine(
+                    inherited_next,
+                    *(
+                        self.combine(self.regions.get(line), self.get(line))
+                        for line in range(start, end + 1)
+                    ),
+                )
+                for line in range(start, end + 1):
+                    self.statement_lines[line] = self.combine(
+                        self.statement_lines.get(line), statement_tests
+                    )
+            self.node_suppressions[node] = statement_tests
+            for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
+                visit(child, statement_tests, inherited_next)
+
+        visit(tree)
+
+    def for_context(self, context, result=None):
+        node = context.get("node")
+        suppression = self.node_suppressions.get(node)
+        # File checks have no AST node, but may report a physical line.
+        if result is not None:
+            suppression = self.combine(
+                suppression, self.regions.get(result.lineno)
+            )
+            if node is None:
+                suppression = self.combine(
+                    suppression, self.statement_lines.get(result.lineno)
+                )
+        return suppression

+def combine_nosec(*suppressions):
+    """Union test sets, distinguishing blanket from absent suppressions."""
+    combined = None
+    for suppression in suppressions:
+        if suppression is not None:
+            if not suppression:
+                return set()
+            if combined is None:
+                combined = set()
+            combined.update(suppression)
+    return combined

+To suppress a region, use ``# nosec-begin`` and ``# nosec-end``:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin B602, B607
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/ls *', shell=True)
+  subprocess.Popen('/bin/echo *', shell=True)
+  # nosec-end
+
+The region starts on the physical line after ``nosec-begin`` and ends before
+the line containing ``nosec-end``. Regions may nest; an end closes the most
+recent active region. Unmatched ends do nothing, and text after an end is
+ignored. An indented region automatically closes at a later nonblank line
+with less leading indentation. Otherwise, an unclosed region lasts until
+the end of the file. Indentation is measured from the line's leading
+whitespace, even when a directive follows code.
+
+Use ``# nosec-next-line`` to suppress the next statement:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-next-line subprocess_popen_with_shell_equals_true
+  # An explanatory comment may go here.
+  subprocess.Popen(
+      '/bin/echo',
+      shell=True,
+  )
+
+Blank lines, comments, and lines containing only grouping tokens
+(``(``, ``)``, ``[``, ``]``, ``{``, ``}``), semicolons, or ``...`` are skipped
+when finding the target. Only the first target statement is suppressed,
+including its continuation lines. A target compound statement includes its
+body. A directive after code applies forward, rather than to that code.
+
+Both new directives accept a selector directly after the keyword. Keywords
+are case-insensitive. Omitted or empty selectors and ``all`` suppress all
+enabled tests; ``none`` suppresses nothing. Selectors accept test IDs, test
+names, and ID prefixes with a wildcard, such as ``B60*``. Spaces, commas,
+and ``|`` union test sets. ``&`` intersects sets, ``-`` subtracts sets, and
+``!`` complements a set relative to the enabled tests. Negation binds most
+tightly, followed by intersection and difference (left to right), followed
+by union. Parentheses change grouping, for example:
+
+.. code-block:: python
+
+  # nosec-begin (B60* | assert_used) - B607
+  # nosec-next-line all & !B602
+
+If an expression cannot be parsed, its whitespace- and comma-separated
+tokens are treated as a plain union. A selector resolving to an empty set
+has no effect. Suppressions apply to whole statements: any suppressed line
+of a multiline statement suppresses its findings, even if an end directive
+occurs later in that statement. A region beginning inside a compound
+statement's body does not suppress the earlier header.
+
+Applicable inline, region, and next-statement suppressions are combined.
+A blanket suppression dominates. Resolved suppressions covering all enabled
+tests count toward ``nosec``; other nonempty sets count toward
+``skipped_tests``. Counts increase for each suppressed finding.
+``--ignore-nosec`` disables inline suppressions and all these directives.
+

 -----------------

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import io
+import unittest
+
+from bandit.core import config
+from bandit.core import manager
+from bandit.core import nosec
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+
+class SelectorTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_selectors(self):
+        enabled = {"B101", "B602", "B607"}
+        cases = {
+            "": set(),
+            "  ": set(),
+            "all": set(),
+            "none": None,
+            "B999": None,
+            "assert_used": {"B101"},
+            "B6*": {"B602", "B607"},
+            "B*": set(),
+            "B9*": None,
+            "B101 B602": {"B101", "B602"},
+            "B101, B602": {"B101", "B602"},
+            "B101 | B602 & B607": {"B101"},
+            "(B101 | B602) & B602": {"B602"},
+            "all - B6*": {"B101"},
+            "!B6*": {"B101"},
+            "!(B101 | B602)": {"B607"},
+            "!none": set(),
+            "!all": None,
+            "B101 - B101": None,
+            "none | B602": {"B602"},
+            "B101 & B602": None,
+            "B101 | !B101": set(),
+            "all - B602 - B607": {"B101"},
+            "B101 , , B602": {"B101", "B602"},
+            "B101 &": {"B101"},
+            "( B101 B602": {"B101", "B602"},
+            "B101 invalid:text B602": {"B101", "B602"},
+        }
+        for expression, expected in cases.items():
+            with self.subTest(expression=expression):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    expected, nosec.parse_selector(expression, enabled)
+                )
+
+    def test_combine_blanket_and_specific(self):
+        self.assertEqual(set(), utils.combine_nosec({"B101"}, set()))
+        self.assertEqual(set(), utils.combine_nosec(set(), {"B101"}))
+        self.assertIsNone(utils.combine_nosec(None, None))
+        self.assertEqual(
+            {"B101", "B602"},
+            utils.get_nosec({1: {"B101"}, 2: {"B602"}}, {"linerange": [1, 2]}),
+        )
+
+
+class DirectiveTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def scan(self, source, ignore=False, include=None):
+        scanner = manager.BanditManager(
+            config.BanditConfig(),
+            "file",
+            debug=True,
+            ignore_nosec=ignore,
+            profile={"include": include or []},
+        )
+        scanner._parse_file(
+            "example.py", io.BytesIO(source.encode()), ["example.py"]
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([], scanner.skipped)
+        return (
+            [(r.lineno, r.test_id) for r in scanner.results],
+            scanner.metrics.data["example.py"],
+        )
+
+    def test_region_boundaries_and_case(self):
+        issues, metrics = self.scan(
+            "assert True # NoSeC-BeGiN B101\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+            "assert True # NOSEC-END ignored B602\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(1, "B101"), (3, "B101"), (4, "B101")], issues)
+        self.assertEqual(1, metrics["skipped_tests"])
+        self.assertEqual(0, metrics["nosec"])
+
+    def test_nested_regions_union_and_end_stack(self):
+        issues, _ = self.scan(
+            "# nosec-end\n"
+            "# nosec-begin B101\n"
+            "# nosec-begin B307\n"
+            "assert eval('1')\n"
+            "# nosec-end trailing explanation\n"
+            "assert eval('1')\n"
+            "# nosec-end\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(6, "B307"), (8, "B101")], issues)
+
+    def test_dedent_and_leading_whitespace(self):
+        issues, _ = self.scan(
+            "def f():\n"
+            "    value = 1 # nosec-begin B101\n"
+            "    assert True\n"
+            "    if value:\n"
+            "        # nosec-begin B307\n"
+            "        assert eval('1')\n"
+            "    assert eval('1')\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(7, "B307"), (8, "B101")], issues)
+
+    def test_tab_indentation(self):
+        issues, _ = self.scan(
+            "def f():\n\t# nosec-begin\n\tassert True\nassert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(4, "B101")], issues)
+
+    def test_tabs_after_code_do_not_change_region_indentation(self):
+        issues, _ = self.scan(
+            "def f():\n    x\t= 1 # nosec-begin B101\n"
+            "    assert True\nassert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(4, "B101")], issues)
+
+    def test_unterminated_global_region(self):
+        issues, metrics = self.scan(
+            "# nosec-begin\nassert True\nassert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([], issues)
+        self.assertEqual(2, metrics["nosec"])
+
+    def test_next_statement_skips_trivia(self):
+        issues, _ = self.scan(
+            "# NoSeC-NeXt-LiNe assert_used\n"
+            "\n# comment\n...\n()\n[]\n{}\n"
+            "assert (\n    True\n)\n"
+            "assert True\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(11, "B101")], issues)
+
+    def test_next_statement_only_first_semicolon_statement(self):
+        issues, metrics = self.scan(
+            "# nosec-next-line B101\nassert True; assert False\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual([(2, "B101")], issues)
+        self.assertEqual(1, metrics["skipped_tests"])
+
